mods.name: ModUpdater
mods.description:
The in-game mod manager (F7): browse mods from the sources you watch, install, update and disable them, and see what other players have.

What it does
- My mods lists what you have, updates first. Browse shows everything your sources offer, grouped by source.
- Players shows who has which mods, and the mods other players have that you do not.
- Sources: the main repos are built in, community sources come from pull requests to the manager's repo, and you can add your own.
- Mod settings: change any loaded mod's settings in the game (switches, sliders, numbers, keys and colours), with a reset button for each.
- Mods reload in-game with no restart; ones that cannot say so.
mods.notes: 2.13.0: Auto update. Switch it on for a mod in My mods, and turn on 'Update mods automatically' in the Manager tab: every few minutes (5 by default, at least 2) the manager looks for new versions of those mods and updates them one at a time, 20 seconds apart, the manager itself last. Mods that need a restart are downloaded and wait for it. Only installed, switched-on mods are touched (nothing new is installed, nothing downgraded, disabled mods stay off), and nothing runs on a loading screen, while dead, teleporting or in a cutscene. The timed look reads only each source's manifest.json from raw.githubusercontent.com (not counted against GitHub's 60-requests-an-hour limit without a login, and with an ETag); a full check only follows a real new version, and a 403/429 pauses automatic checks (doubling, up to an hour, or as long as GitHub asks).
